stories.headline: United States and Denmark reach new security agreement for Greenland
stories.body:
The United States and Denmark announced a security agreement regarding Greenland to resolve a diplomatic dispute [c1].

US President Donald Trump wrote about the agreement on social media [c2]. He said Denmark will grant the US permanent control over security in Greenland [c2]. He said Denmark will grant control over all other needs [c2]. Trump added that this control will come at no cost to the United States [c2].

Leaders plan to sign the security deal next week [c3]. They expect to sign it at the UN General Assembly [c3]. The agreement involves the US, Denmark, and Greenland [c3].

An official from the US State Department spoke about the agreement rules [c4]. The official said non-NATO countries cannot build military bases in Greenland [c4]. Non-NATO countries also cannot invest in sensitive sectors under the deal [c4].

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen spoke about the agreement [c5]. Frederiksen said the deal strengthens common security in the Arctic [c5]. She said it strengthens security in the North Atlantic [c5]. She said it recognizes the sovereignty of Denmark [c5]. She said it recognizes the territorial integrity of Denmark [c5]. She said it recognizes the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination [c5].

French President Emmanuel Macron commented on the deal [c6]. Macron said the agreement reaffirms Danish sovereignty over Greenland [c6]. He said the deal respects international law [c6].

Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen praised the deal [c7]. Rasmussen called it a binding agreement [c7]. He said it strengthens security while respecting Denmark's red lines [c7].

Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen also spoke [c8]. Nielsen said the agreement recognizes Greenland's interests [c8]. He said the deal benefits all parties [c8].

Greenland has a population of roughly 56,000 residents [c9]. More than two-thirds of its territory lies within the Arctic Circle [c9].

The United States already operates a base in Greenland [c10]. It runs Pituffik Space Base in northwestern Greenland [c10]. The US operates the base under the Defense of Greenland Treaty [c10]. That treaty was signed in 1951 [c10].

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised the new agreement [c11]. Rubio called the agreement a historic deal [c11]. He said it completely addresses US national security concerns [c11].

Donald Trump first suggested buying Greenland from Denmark in 2019 [c12]. He suggested buying the island during his first term as US president [c12]. In January 2026, Trump indicated the US could use force to seize Greenland [c13].

vocab.meaning: the independent power of a country to govern itself
relating to the land or area belonging to a country
the state of being whole and undivided
an agreement that must legally be obeyed

stories.headline: Donald Trump plans to create AI Force and name new AI czar
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump announced plans to form an AI Force [c14]. Trump also plans to appoint an artificial intelligence czar [c14].

Trump said artificial intelligence could become a large part of the national economy [c15]. He said AI could eventually account for 25% of the United States' GDP [c15].

Trump posted about the new czar position on social media [c18]. He said candidates for the AI czar position must have a high IQ [c18].

Former US AI czar David Sacks resigned earlier in the year [c21]. Sacks currently chairs Trump's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology [c21].

Trump said his administration will not stifle the growth of the AI industry [c24]. He said officials will use existing criminal and civil laws to target bad actors [c24].

Several tech executives want a slowdown or regulations in AI development [c16]. These leaders include Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Sam Altman of OpenAI, and Elon Musk of xAI [c16]. An Anthropic researcher warned that AI companies are gambling with lives [c20]. The researcher warned AI could pose existential risks by the end of the decade [c20].

California Governor Gavin Newsom announced plans for an AI safety panel [c19]. The panel will develop safety regulations, including a potential kill switch [c19].

Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping plan to meet at the White House on September 24 [c23]. They are expected to discuss AI competition [c23].

vocab.meaning: relating to threat to the very survival of humanity
to prevent something from growing or developing

stories.headline: Houthi rebels target Riyadh with missiles, disrupting flights
stories.body:
Iran-backed Houthi militants launched drone and missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia [c25]. They targeted the capital city of Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu [c25].

Black smoke rose from fuel tanks near King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh [c26]. The attack caused temporary flight delays and cancellations [c26].

Saudi authorities intercepted a ballistic missile over Riyadh [c27]. They stopped aerial attempts over Bish, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu [c27].

Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea spoke about the strikes [c28]. He said the attacks responded to 300 Saudi strikes in Yemen over the past week [c28].

Fighting between Houthis and government forces killed 48 people on Saturday [c29]. The dead included 31 Houthi fighters and 17 government soldiers [c29].

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Turkiye would consider supporting Saudi Arabia [c30]. Support would come under a defence pact signed in Mecca on August 7 [c30].

Pakistani Lieutenant-General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan will physically defend Saudi Arabia [c31]. Defense would happen under the Mecca Defence Alliance [c31].

The UN reported that renewed fighting displaced over 112,000 people [c32]. The UN Security Council condemned Houthi attacks on civilian energy infrastructure [c35].

vocab.meaning: stopped or caught something before it reached its destination
basic physical systems such as power networks and transportation

stories.headline: United States enacts law to place high tariffs on Russian oil buyers
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump signed a new trade bill into law on Friday, September 18, 2026 [c44]. The White House confirmed that Trump signed H.R. 5334 [c44]. The official name of the law is the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, 2026 [c37].

The new law permits the United States to punish certain countries [c38]. It permits the US to impose a 100% tariff on goods from target nations [c38]. This tariff applies to countries that continue importing crude oil or natural gas from Russia [c38]. The tax takes effect 30 days after enactment [c38].

The bill received strong support in the US Congress [c45]. The US Senate passed the legislation in August with an 86 to 11 vote [c45]. The House of Representatives passed the measure by a vote of 262 to 159 [c45].

Republican Senator Lindsey Graham spearheaded the legislation [c46]. Senator Graham died in July 2026 [c46].

The law was originally created to stop funding for Russia's war in Ukraine [c39]. It targeted top Russian leadership and energy customers [c39]. Lawmakers later amended the bill text [c40]. The new text extended sanctions on Iran for another five years until 2031 [c40].

India relies heavily on Russian energy supplies [c41]. Russia accounted for more than 51% of India's crude oil imports in July 2026 [c41]. India's imports of Russian oil hit a 38-month low in December 2025 [c49]. Imports then reached an 11-month high in April 2026 after the US and Israel war on Iran [c49].

India already faces other US trade tariffs [c42]. India faces a 10% tariff under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 [c42]. It faces a 50% tariff under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 [c42].

The Trump administration previously put a 25% punitive tariff on India in August 2025 over Russian oil [c48]. Trump removed that tariff in February 2026 after an interim trade deal [c48].

Indian leaders criticized the new US law [c43]. Union Minister of State Kirti Vardhan Singh said India considers the US tariffs very unfair [c43]. Singh said India will buy energy from viable sources independently [c43]. India's Ministry of External Affairs said New Delhi is committed to energy security through diversified sourcing [c47].

vocab.meaning: imposing penalties or punishment on a nation
a tax placed by a government on imported goods
varied or drawn from several different sources

stories.headline: ABVP candidate group wins top posts in Delhi University elections
stories.body:
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad student group won three top posts in student elections at Delhi University [c50]. The ABVP captured three central panel posts in the DUSU elections [c50].

ABVP candidate Yash Dabas was elected DUSU president with 24,576 votes [c52]. He defeated NSUI candidate Vijay Shankar Meena, who received 22,523 votes [c52]. Dabas is an international tennis player who represented the university at major games [c62]. He completed his undergraduate degree at Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Khalsa College [c63]. He is pursuing an MA in Buddhist Studies at Delhi University [c63]. Dabas said his priority is conducting safety audits of college hostels [c64].

Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen won the vice-presidential post with 30,615 votes [c51]. He defeated ABVP's Ishu Maurya, who received 16,901 votes [c51]. Shokeen ran as an independent candidate after NSUI denied him a ticket on September 11 [c58]. His father works as a bus conductor, and his mother works as an Anganwadi teacher [c59].

ABVP candidate Riya Chhawdi won the secretary post with 21,650 votes [c53]. ABVP's Lakshay Raj Singh won the joint secretary post by 837 votes [c54].

The National Students' Union of India drew a blank in the central panel elections [c56]. Overall voter turnout was 40.46% [c55]. Union Home Minister Amit Shah congratulated the ABVP on the victory [c57].

vocab.meaning: a official group or slate of positions in an election
